x: The 1 Mile saw Harry Shields, Syd Jarlett and Bill Speaight opposed to two Whitgift boys, and they naturally finished well ahead of the schoolboys.

However, the result mattered little so long as all those competing enjoyed their sport, and actually the 2 Miles field was reminiscent of the Cross Country season with such as, Les Cohen, Bill Speaight, Harry Shields, Alf Taylor, Dick Tobin, Tom Morrell.
Bill Speaight, having been on duty the previous night, was not up to the mark, and retired after the first lap, and Andy Gray twisted his ankle in the last lap and limped back home.

Bert Shaw was 6th, Carter 7th, Beer 9th, Morrell 10th, Shields 16th, Walker 18th, Penny 21st, Tobin 22nd, Taylor 23rd, and Jannaway 29th. In the Closed Events, Syd Jarlett, Bill Speaight and Alf Bishop were amongst the prizewinners. Fulham A.R.P. 1st July, at Stamford Bridge.
Bill Speaight suffered from leg strain last season and gave up racing this winter. He had started training again and is looking very fit.

Jim Heathfield was second in the 440 and Terry Bateman won the high jump. Tea and sandwiches were provided afterwards by our hosts, prominent among whom were our old friends Syd Jarlett and Bill Speaight..
Bill Speaight, a veteran and second claim member was an easy winner of the handicap, with Len Rolls another vet. second and young Gowar, a lad who looks about 20 but is only 16, 3rd.
